displayName: Acme stock-reservation service (UniBasic → Java 21 / Spring Boot 3, feasibility POC)
description: Feasibility POC for a prospective client engagement: an equipment-finance ILS system, business logic in Rocket UniData/UniBasic, target Java 17+/PostgreSQL. Translates reserve-stock.pick, an AUTHORED representative sample (NOT sourced from a public repository) written to exercise the READU...LOCKED / RELEASE record-locking idiom that the small public calibration corpus (github.com/zelenko/pick) does not contain. From a signed unibasic spec (targetStack=java-spring): the three-way OPEN/READU outcome (found-and-locked / locked-by-another-user / not-found) becomes a sealed LockOutcome result type (LockOutcome, StockReservationService); the strictly-less-than stock guard and per-exit-path RELEASE become normal Java exceptions and transaction-boundary semantics rather than a manually-tracked release call. Builds OFFLINE through the maven-sidecar (pinned plugins + junit/assertj only). UniData/UniVerse have no free/scriptable runtime, so source-execution equivalence is NOT claimed — the golden score + this compiling, passing JUnit suite are the gates, the same honest posture as the OpenEdge ABL and canonical-unibasic-branch-service archetypes. A genuine client engagement must validate the exact locking semantics against the client's real UniData source before this ships.
